# Empirical strategy {#sec-strategy}

```{python}
#| include: false
import pandas as pd
import _helpers as H

pw = H.prereg_power()
```

This chapter specifies the estimand, the model, the estimator, the inference procedure, the multiplicity control and the interpretation rule, reports the power analysis and what it implies, and documents the pre-registration and freeze. It describes what was frozen on `{python} H.fact("tag")`; later chapters report what was found.

## Estimand and model M1 {#sec-m1}

For country $i$ and year $t$, with country effects $\alpha_i$ and year effects $\lambda_t$, the confirmatory model M1 is

$$
\begin{aligned}
\text{CAPB}_{it} ={}& \alpha_i + \lambda_t + \beta_S\,W^S_{it} + \beta_E\,W^E_{it} + \beta_U\,W^U_{it} + \rho_P\,\text{Post}_{it} \\
& + \gamma_B\,W^S_{it}\,\bar a_i + \gamma_W\,W^S_{it}\,\tilde a_{it} + \eta\,a_{it} + \sum_{e}\theta_e\,W^S_{it}\,(\text{era}_{e,t} - m_e) + \varepsilon_{it},
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-m1}

where $a_{it}$ is the lagged old-age dependency ratio standardised on the estimation sample, $\bar a_i$ is its country mean over that sample, and $\tilde a_{it} = a_{it} - \bar a_i$ is the within-country deviation. The coefficient $\rho_P$ on the post-election share is written $\rho$ in the pre-registration; we reserve $\rho$ for persistence below. The two interaction regressors are each divided by the standard deviation of their component, so that $\gamma_B$ and $\gamma_W$ are effects per +1 SD of the between and the within component (about 3.2 pp of OLDDEP1 each). The delayed-election regressor $W^D$ is identically zero in the sample and is dropped automatically.

*Era terms.* The association of elections with the CAPB may have changed across the pre-crisis, crisis and recovery periods. M1 therefore includes interactions of $W^S$ with indicators for 2008--2015 and 2016--2021 (reference 1995--2007), each centred at its exposure-weighted mean $m_e = \sum W^S \cdot \text{era}_e / \sum W^S$. Because of the centring, $\beta_S$ is the association at the average era composition of scheduled-election exposure, and not the 1995--2007 association that uncentred terms would give.

*No controls.* The primary model has no controls. Contemporaneous macroeconomic variables are potential mediators (election-driven fiscal expansion can move them), and lagged controls added nothing to power (@sec-estimator). The lagged output gap and euro-area membership enter only in a robustness model on 703 rows.

*Interpretation of $\beta_S$.* $\beta_S$ is the conditional association of a full year (that is, $W^S = 1$) of pre-election exposure to a scheduled election with the CAPB, in percentage points of potential GDP, at the sample-average moderator. It is a conditional association with a predetermined exposure. Scheduled elections are predetermined, not exogenous ([Chapter 7](#sec-limitations)), and neither $\beta_S$ nor the interaction coefficients are given a causal reading.

## The within-between split of ageing {#sec-mundlak}

Decomposing $a_{it}$ into $\bar a_i$ and $\tilde a_{it}$ follows the correlated-random-effects logic of @mundlak1978 and the within-between formulation of @bell2015. It separates two questions that a single interaction would conflate: whether election associations differ between countries that are older or younger on average ($\gamma_B$, a cross-country contrast that can be confounded by other country traits), and whether the association changes as a given country ages relative to its own mean ($\gamma_W$). The pre-registered expectation is that $\gamma_B$ is better identified than $\gamma_W$, because within-country variation is small once year effects are removed (@sec-moderator). Interaction diagnostics (binned linearity and common support) follow @hainmueller2019 and are reported as part of the diagnostics.

## Estimator V7 {#sec-estimator}

The estimator, called V7, is a feasible weighted least squares with AR(1) feasible generalised least squares and fixed effects. It was selected before any effect estimate was computed, by a pre-specified mechanical rule applied to power simulations (the rule is: among variants with a wild-bootstrap size of 3.5--6.5% and small bias, take the one with the smallest minimum detectable effect for $\beta_S$ at the estimated persistence, breaking ties of 5% or less in favour of the simplest). The steps are repeated unchanged inside every bootstrap sample:

1. *First stage.* Fixed-effects OLS of the CAPB on the full M1 design gives residuals $\hat u^{(1)}_{it}$.
2. *Weights.* $w_i = 1/\hat\sigma_i^2$, where $\hat\sigma_i^2$ is the mean squared first-stage residual of country $i$. This addresses groupwise heteroskedasticity, which is severe in this panel (the residual standard deviation ranges from about 1 to about 5 pp, with Ireland the largest).
3. *Persistence.* The pooled AR(1) coefficient $\phi$ of the country-standardised first-stage residuals over consecutive years is estimated and then corrected analytically for the bias of the within estimator [@nickell1981].
4. *GLS.* A Prais--Winsten transformation with $\hat\phi$, weighted by $w_i$, followed by generalised least squares. Standard errors are CR1 cluster-robust by country.

The mechanical selection found that the gain in power came from the estimator, not from controls: V7 has a $\beta_S$ minimum detectable effect of about 0.51 pp against about 0.70 pp for plain two-way fixed-effects OLS. We deliberately do not use a lagged dependent variable or difference/system GMM: with T = 27 the Nickell bias is modest, and instrument proliferation makes GMM fragile [@roodman2009]. The costs of V7 are that the weights and $\hat\phi$ are estimated, which is why they are re-estimated in every bootstrap sample, and that the AR(1) correction was calibrated at persistence of about 0.7 and was not validated at much higher persistence (relevant to some secondary outcomes, @sec-secondary).

## Inference {#sec-inference}

With 27 clusters, asymptotic cluster-robust inference is unreliable, and for V7 the CR1 $t(26)$ test over-rejects by about 8--10% in simulation; it is shown for transparency only. Confirmatory $p$-values come from a null-imposed wild-cluster bootstrap-$t$ by country [@cameron2008; @roodman2019] with Rademacher weights, B = 9,999 replications, and the whole feasible procedure re-estimated in each bootstrap sample. The two-sided $p$-value is $(1 + \#\{|t^*| \ge |t|\})/(B+1)$. Intervals are 95% bootstrap-$t$ percentile intervals from the unrestricted wild bootstrap with the same weights and $B$. Test-inversion intervals would be preferable in principle but are computationally prohibitive; their absence is a limitation. The seed is 42 through the project's seed scheme.

The known limitation of this procedure is that, under block-bootstrap noise that carries real cross-country co-movement, the wild-bootstrap size for $\beta_S$ was about `{python} H.fact("wcb_size")`% against a nominal 5% in simulation, so $p$-values may be too small if cross-country dependence is real. Driscoll--Kraay standard errors [@driscoll1998] and common-correlated-effects augmentation [@pesaran2006], together with a test of residual cross-sectional dependence [@pesaran2015], accompany the headline as pre-specified sensitivities.

## Multiplicity {#sec-multiplicity}

The confirmatory family is {H1, H2B}, adjusted by Holm's step-down procedure at a familywise level of 0.05. The ten secondary $\beta_S$ tests are adjusted by the Benjamini--Hochberg procedure [@bh1995] at $q = 0.05$, with the Benjamini--Yekutieli adjustment shown beside it as a conservative check, because the outcomes are strongly related and BH assumes independence or positive dependence. Everything else is descriptive or exploratory.

## Smallest effect size of interest and the three-way reading {#sec-sesoi}

Statistical significance alone does not say whether an association is large enough to matter. Each confirmatory interval is therefore read three ways, and both flags are reported: it *excludes zero* if the 95% interval does not contain zero; it is *equivalent* if the interval lies inside $\pm\delta$; otherwise it is *inconclusive*. The label precedence is "excludes zero", then "equivalent", then "inconclusive". The smallest effect size of interest (SESOI) is $\delta$ = `{python} H.num(H.sesoi(), 1)` pp of potential GDP (per SD for $\gamma_B$), confirmed by the researcher on 2026-10-12. It lies between two literature benchmarks: 0.41 pp, the coefficient in @bednar2019 for the WEO structural balance, and 0.49 pp, the expenditure effect around regular elections in @afonso2026. Because we require the whole 95% interval (rather than a 90% interval, as in a conventional two one-sided tests procedure) to lie inside the band, the equivalence criterion is conservative.

Two cautions attach to the rule. First, the typical first-outturn revision of the CAPB was pre-registered as `{python} H.fact("revision")` pp, "as large as the SESOI". The post-run description ([Appendix E](#sec-app-revisions)) is more careful: the mean absolute revision is `{python} H.s4_ci("mean_abs_revision")` pp and the median absolute revision `{python} H.s4_ci("median_abs_revision")` pp, so the typical revision does not demonstrably exceed the SESOI, although revisions of that size are common (`{python} H.s4_ci("share_abs_gt_sesoi", 0, True)` of country-years exceed 0.5 pp). Measurement error is stated beside every result ([Chapter 7](#sec-limitations)). Second, the SESOI is a judgement, set before the analysis, not a derived quantity.

## Power and what it implies {#sec-power}

```{python}
#| label: tbl-power
#| tbl-cap: "Minimum detectable effects (wild bootstrap, 80% power, alpha = 0.05; pp of potential GDP; per SD for the ageing interactions). Source: pre-registration, section 8 (Gate 3d)."
rows = []
for key, lab in [("beta_S", "$\\beta_S$"), ("gamma_B", "$\\gamma_B$ (per SD)"), ("gamma_W", "$\\gamma_W$ (per SD)")]:
    r = pw.get(key, {})
    rows.append({"Target": lab, "At estimated persistence ($\\rho \\approx 0.69$)": H.num(r.get("rho"), 3), "With no persistence": H.num(r.get("rho0"), 3), "Gate verdict": r.get("g2", H.NA)})
H.show_table(pd.DataFrame(rows), widths=[22, 30, 20, 16])
```

@tbl-power gives the minimum detectable effects from the Gate 3d simulation on the real election calendar. They exceed both literature benchmarks for $\beta_S$ unless persistence is as estimated: power against 0.41 pp is `{python} H.num(pw.get("power", {}).get("p41"), 1)`% at the estimated persistence (`{python} H.num(pw.get("power", {}).get("p41_0"), 1)`% with none) and against 0.49 pp `{python} H.num(pw.get("power", {}).get("p49"), 1)`% (`{python} H.num(pw.get("power", {}).get("p49_0"), 1)`%). Three implications follow. An inconclusive result is the most likely outcome, and it is a legitimate finding; it is not a failure of the design. Because $\gamma_W$ is not powered (its minimum detectable effect exceeds 1 pp per SD), it is reported descriptively, by the pre-registered demotion rule. And, as a general property of significance filtering, an estimate that clears the filter near or below the detectable threshold is likely to overstate the true association (the "winner's curse"); this is relevant to the headline estimate ([Chapter 6](#sec-discussion)).

## Diagnostics and robustness plan {#sec-plan}

Pre-registered diagnostics are reported and never used to select a specification: modified Wald test for groupwise heteroskedasticity, the Wooldridge serial-correlation test, the Pesaran cross-sectional dependence test, CIPS panel unit-root tests [@pesaran2007] on the CAPB and the moderator, variance inflation factors (above 5 flagged), a Hausman comparison alongside the Mundlak terms [@hausman1978], binned linearity and common support for the interactions, and a lead placebo that adds the share of year $t$ inside months 13--24 before a scheduled election. Details of the robustness definitions were fixed in `docs/robustness_spec.md` after the confirmatory result and before any robustness result was computed; they define the inference sensitivities (OLS baseline, Driscoll--Kraay with two bandwidths, two-way clustering, two CCE designs), sample variants (balanced panel, dropping unclassified or delayed elections, gap-filled classes, leave-one-country-out, Ireland 2010 winsorised, crisis exclusions, the 2022 extension, the controls model) and definition variants (6- and 18-month windows, a calendar-year dummy, alternative moderators). Every specification is reported whatever it shows. No specification is selected or ranked, and counts of specifications are descriptive, not a vote.

## Pre-registration and freeze {#sec-freeze}

The pre-registration (`docs/preregistration.md`) fixes the question, hypotheses, sample, exposure, model, estimator, inference, interpretation rule and the set of secondary analyses. It became binding when the git tag `{python} H.fact("tag")` was created on commit `{python} H.fact("tag_commit")`, which contains it and a manifest of SHA-256 hashes of the registry, the code that defines the confirmatory quantities, the pinned raw-data manifests and the analysis extract. The freeze script verifies nine checks before tagging, and the confirmatory runner refuses to run on the real panel unless the tag exists.

| Date | Event |
|:-------------|:--------------------------------------------------------------|
| 2026-10-12 | Tag created; manifest and extract hash recorded in the tag message |
| 2026-10-12 | Tag pushed to the public repository **before** any analysis of the real outcome |
| 2026-10-12 | Confirmatory analysis run once (B = 9,999, seed 42); provenance verified against the manifest |
| 2026-10-12 | Robustness and diagnostics specification committed before the suite was run |
| 2026-10-13 | Secondary-outcomes specification committed before its analysis; analysis run |

: Order of events after the freeze (`docs/post_freeze_log.md`) {#tbl-timeline}

The robustness and secondary specifications are not part of the frozen manifest. The secondary analyses were pre-specified as a family in the pre-registration (section 10); the later specification documents fix details left open there, and are labelled as such. They changed no pre-registered quantity.

## What was seen before the freeze, and deviations {#sec-disclosure}

Before the freeze, the outcome series was used for sample coverage, for unconditional descriptive statistics, and for residual-based noise calibration of the power studies (persistence, country variance heterogeneity and the Ireland 2010 outlier). The choice of estimator was informed by that noise structure, never by any estimate of an election or ageing effect. No statistic relating the outcome to any election variable had been computed. During the construction of the calendar, file dimensions and coverage years of the CAPB file were printed before the exposure code was final, but no CAPB value informed any classification or window.

**Deviations from the pre-registration: none.** The amendments file that the pre-registration provides for was not needed. One test file that asserted the pre-tag state was made tag-aware after the confirmatory run; it is not part of the freeze manifest and changed no pre-registered quantity.
